question: If the marked price of a book is ₹900, then find the selling price of the book after getting discount of 13%
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

SP = 900 × (100 − 13)%

SP = 900 × 87%

SP = 9 × 87 = 783

**∴ The correct answer is ₹783.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the book = ₹900

Discount offered = 13%

**Formula Used:**

Discount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × MP

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

 MP ₹900 
• 
 −13% Discount (−₹117) SP ₹783 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount amount = 13% of 900

⇒ Discount = (13 ÷ 100) × 900 = ₹117

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 900 − 117

⇒ Selling Price = ₹783

**∴ The correct answer is ₹783.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is fundamentally a reduction applied to the Marked Price of an article. It is always calculated on the MP unless specified otherwise. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are applied on a product, the effective single discount percentage is calculated using the formula: [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Profit and Loss Relationship

While Discount is calculated on MP, Profit and Loss are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP). A dealer offers a discount on MP to arrive at the SP, and the difference between SP and CP determines the actual profit or loss.
